avoid:Vin Jaune on a café terrace.name: Vin Jaune on a café terrace
avoid:Vin Jaune on a café terrace.teaser: If the 'vin jaune' on the terrace list comes from a 75 cl bottle, it is not Vin Jaune
avoid:Vin Jaune on a café terrace.story: Under the arcades the café boards chalk up 'vin jaune' by the glass, and nobody brings the bottle to the table. That is the problem. Vin Jaune may only be sold in one bottle: the squat 62 cl clavelin, reserved by the appellation rules for the Vin Jaune of Arbois, Côtes du Jura, L'Étoile and Château-Chalon. A pour from a tall 75 cl bottle is something else, often an oxidative Savagnin, a good wine in its own right but not the one on the board. The real thing smells of walnut and curry and is best met with the person who made it.
avoid:Vin Jaune on a café terrace.why: Ask to see the bottle: no clavelin, no Vin Jaune, whatever the board says.
facts: Look for the short-necked 62 cl clavelin on the table or the shelf before you order a glass
Taste it at the Caveau des Jacobins in Lons, where the caviste pours from the clavelin, or at the source with Domaine Macle in Château-Chalon

avoid:Comté in plastic.name: Comté in plastic
avoid:Comté in plastic.teaser: A vacuum-packed wedge with no age and no affineur teaches you nothing about Comté
avoid:Comté in plastic.story: The souvenir cellars stack pre-cut wedges of Comté in plastic by the till, often young wheels from large-scale affinage, sold with no age on the label and no name behind it. Comté changes completely with time and with the cellar it ripened in: a young piece is milky and soft, an old one dry, nutty and crunchy with crystals. A single anonymous wedge cannot show you that. A fromager-affineur cuts from the wheel in front of you, tells you how many months it has, and lets you taste before you pay.
avoid:Comté in plastic.why: Taste three ages side by side, cut to order, before you buy any of them.
facts: Check the wedge's label for an age in months and the affineur's name; if both are missing, put it back
Fromagerie Vagne under the rue du Commerce arcades, or the cheese stalls at the Thursday market in Lons

avoid:Jeunet in Arbois.name: Jeunet in Arbois
avoid:Jeunet in Arbois.teaser: The two stars left Arbois's rue de l'Hôtel de Ville in 2021; old guides still send diners there
avoid:Jeunet in Arbois.story: Jean-Paul Jeunet announced his retirement in February 2016 and handed the kitchen of the Arbois restaurant to his second, Steven Naessens, who ran it as Maison Jeunet. In November 2021 Naessens took the name and the two Michelin stars out of town to the Château de Germigney at Port-Lesney. The old house in Arbois, a former Carmelite convent of 1643 that became the Hôtel de Paris, was taken over by the owner of Germigney and renamed Carmel 1643 (reported 2023). Plenty of printed guides, this one's earlier edition included, still give the Arbois address for the starred dinner.
avoid:Jeunet in Arbois.why: Book the two-star meal at Port-Lesney, not in Arbois, and check the address on the confirmation.
facts: At 9 rue de l'Hôtel de Ville in Arbois you will find the Carmel 1643 building, not the two-star restaurant (2023 report)
Maison Jeunet par Steven Naessens at the Château de Germigney, Port-Lesney

follow:Jura tourism.name: Jura tourism
follow:Jura tourism.teaser: The département's tourist board: fruitière visits, craft workshops and the week's agenda
follow:Jura tourism.story: Jura Tourisme, the département's tourism agency, runs jura-tourism.com, and its value for a shore day is the agenda and the listings behind the brochures. That is where the fruitière visits on the plateau are posted with their days and booking rules, alongside the Haut-Jura craft workshops, the pipe-makers of Saint-Claude and the wood courses at Ravilloles. In late autumn it is also the quickest place to see which museums and sites have moved to winter hours or closed until spring. Read it the evening before, since a listing changes faster than any guide.
follow:Jura tourism.why: Check winter opening before you drive: from November many Jura sites shorten their hours or shut.
facts: The official tourism site of the Jura département (Jura Tourisme), with listings and an events agenda

follow:Saline Royale.name: Saline Royale
follow:Saline Royale.teaser: The Arc-et-Senans saltworks' own site: opening hours, exhibitions and the garden season
follow:Saline Royale.story: The Saline Royale d'Arc-et-Senans, the UNESCO-listed royal saltworks east of the vineyard, publishes its own site, and it is the one to trust for what changes: the opening times by season, the temporary exhibitions in the old salt buildings, the garden festival in the warm months, and the concerts and events held inside the semicircle. It also lists the guided tours and the ticket prices for the current year. Look at it before a late-autumn visit, when the hours are shorter and the gardens past their best.
follow:Saline Royale.why: Read the hours page for the week you go; the winter timetable is not the summer one.
facts: The official site of the Saline Royale d'Arc-et-Senans: visits, exhibitions, events
The practical page for hours and prices, and the exhibitions and events pages

follow:Vins du Jura (CIVJ).name: Vins du Jura (CIVJ)
follow:Vins du Jura (CIVJ).teaser: The Jura wine trade body's site: the appellations, the grapes and the dates of the Percée
follow:Vins du Jura (CIVJ).story: The Comité Interprofessionnel des Vins du Jura brings growers and merchants of a small vineyard, about 2,000 hectares, under one roof; its presidency alternates every three years between the two. Its site jura-vins.com sets out each appellation, from Arbois to Château-Chalon, with the grapes and the wine styles, and carries the wine news of the region, the Percée du Vin Jaune included. In 2026 the first two Jura appellations, Arbois and Château-Chalon, mark ninety years. Open the appellation page before a tasting and the names on the labels start to make sense.
follow:Vins du Jura (CIVJ).why: Read the appellation pages the night before a cellar visit; the grower will talk faster than you can take notes.
facts: The official site of the Jura wine interprofession (CIVJ): appellations, grapes, events

follow:Comté (CIGC).name: Comté (CIGC)
follow:Comté (CIGC).teaser: The Comté interprofession's site: the rules, the fruitières and the routes to visit them
follow:Comté (CIGC).story: The Comité Interprofessionnel de Gestion du Comté speaks for the farmers, the village dairies and the affineurs who make the cheese, and its site comte.com is where the rules of the AOP are explained in plain terms: the cows, the pasture, the raw milk, the months in the cellar. It also points visitors towards the fruitières and the cellars that open their doors, and announces the Comté fêtes. Use it to find a dairy on the plateau that takes visitors in the week you are inland.
follow:Comté (CIGC).why: Look up the fruitières open to visitors before driving up to the plateau.

listening:No hi-fi listening bar.name: No hi-fi listening bar
listening:No hi-fi listening bar.teaser: No listening bar in Lons, and none we could find in Besançon either
listening:No hi-fi listening bar.story: A listening bar, in the sense the word now carries, is a room built round a serious sound system and a wall of records, where people come to hear albums played through rather than to talk over them. We looked for one in Lons-le-Saunier and in Besançon in October 2026 and found none; in France such rooms are still a big-city idea. The Jura's evening is a different pleasure: a cold cellar, a clavelin opened by someone who can explain it, or a loud night at the town's own concert hall on the edge of the centre.
listening:No hi-fi listening bar.why: Trade the turntable for the counter, or for the concert hall on a show night.
facts: An evening glass at a counter where the person pouring knows the grower
The Caveau des Jacobins for the glass, or a concert at Le Bœuf sur le Toit

listening:Le Bœuf sur le Toit.name: Le Bœuf sur le Toit
listening:Le Bœuf sur le Toit.teaser: Lons's own concert hall: rap, rock and comedy, with a run of big names in late November
listening:Le Bœuf sur le Toit.story: When Lons gets loud, it is here, at the concert hall on Place du Maréchal Juin. The programme runs from French rap to rock and stand-up, and late November 2026 is full: Elmer Food Beat on Saturday 21 November on their 'Re-Tour', Neg'Marrons on Friday 27 November with 'Le Grand Bilan', the show for their thirty years, and the rap trio 47ter on Saturday 28 November, listed as sold out by one ticket site. Doors open on a crowd of local students and families, beer in plastic cups, and the walk back to the arcades takes minutes.
listening:Le Bœuf sur le Toit.why: Check the date against your shore day; the late-November weekends are when the hall is fullest.
facts: Concerts and comedy most weeks in autumn and winter, usually at 20:30; Elmer Food Beat 21 Nov, Neg'Marrons 27 Nov, 47ter 28 Nov 2026
From EUR 29 for Neg'Marrons, from EUR 32 for 47ter (Oct 2026)

listening:La Rodia, Besançon.name: La Rodia, Besançon
listening:La Rodia, Besançon.teaser: Besançon's state-labelled music hall, an hour north: 1,100 standing under a suspended balcony
listening:La Rodia, Besançon.story: For a bigger night than Lons can give, drive an hour north to Besançon. La Rodia is the city's SMAC, a state-labelled venue for current music, counted among the five busiest in France on its fifth birthday. In 2019 a six-month refit hung a 22-tonne U-shaped balcony in the main hall and raised it to 1,100 places; a smaller room sits beside it. The programme runs from rap and electronic to chanson: in November 2026 the listings carry Camille with 'The Sound of Milk' on the 19th and the rapper Zamdane on the 27th.
listening:La Rodia, Besançon.why: Book the return before you go: the drive back to Lons is an hour on dark roads.
facts: Besançon, about an hour by road north of Lons

craft:Do this one.name: Atelier des Savoir-Faire, Ravilloles
craft:Do this one.teaser: In a village above Saint-Claude, the Haut-Jura's wood trades taught as courses anyone can join
craft:Do this one.story: The Haut-Jura lived for centuries on what its valleys could turn and carve from wood in the long winters: briar pipes at Saint-Claude, toys at Moirans, boxes and small turned objects in every hamlet. At Ravilloles, twelve kilometres from Saint-Claude, the Atelier des Savoir-Faire keeps those trades in use. Local artisans lead creative courses open to all, in wood, metal and decoration, and the wood-turner Lilou Voisinne gave turning demonstrations there in September 2026. You stand at the lathe in the smell of fresh shavings and leave with something you made.
craft:Do this one.why: Book a wood course rather than the exhibition: the point is the lathe, not the showcase.
facts: Creative courses led by local artisans in wood (including an initiation level), metal and decoration; wood-turning demonstrations; children's workshops in the school holidays
From a single workshop to multi-day courses (a four-day course ran in 2022); ask for the winter calendar
Children's workshops EUR 10 each (2026 listings); adult course prices not published, ask when booking

craft:Other one.name: Atelier Genod, Saint-Claude
craft:Other one.teaser: A briar-pipe workshop in Saint-Claude since 1865, where you watch a bowl turned in twenty minutes
craft:Other one.story: Saint-Claude made its name with the briar pipe, and the Genod workshop on the Faubourg Marcel has turned them since 1865. Jacques Craen ran it for decades, opened a shop on the Place de l'Abbaye and began letting visitors into the workshop; Sébastien Beaud took over in 2006 and kept the doors open. The visit is short: a pipe-maker turns a block of briar into a bowl in front of you, between cases of old and carved pipes, and the room smells of hot wood and wax. Missing: you watch a master at work, but there is no class where you make your own.
craft:Other one.why: Go on a weekday morning, when the lathe is running for real work.
facts: A guided demonstration of briar-pipe turning and a display of antique and carved pipes
EUR 3, groups EUR 2.50 a head (May 2024 listing)

craft:Other two.name: Fruitière de Plasne
craft:Other two.teaser: On the plateau above Poligny, a village dairy that lets visitors watch the morning's milk become curd
craft:Other two.story: Comté is still made the old way, in village fruitières where the farmers bring the morning milk and the fromager works it in copper vats. The cooperative Les Délices du Plateau at Plasne, on the plateau above Poligny, takes visitors through the dairy at 8:45 on Wednesday and Friday mornings, about an hour and a half with a commented tasting at the end: steam over the vats, the clean sour smell of whey, the wheels pressed in their moulds. Missing: the visits are listed for August 2026 only, booking is required, and you watch rather than make.
craft:Other two.why: Book a summer morning visit, early, when the curd is being cut.
facts: A guided visit of a working Comté dairy and a commented tasting
Required; Wednesday and Friday mornings, listed for August 2026: ask the Poligny tourist office whether any winter visit is offered

craft:What is sold as Jura-made.name: What is sold as Jura-made
craft:What is sold as Jura-made.teaser: A smoked sausage in a souvenir shop is not a Morteau unless the IGP rules are met
craft:What is sold as Jura-made.story: The shop windows of the old town hang smoked sausages under the Jura's name, and not all of them have earned it. A Saucisse de Morteau IGP is fixed by its specification: a natural, uncoloured pork casing, closed at one end by a small wooden peg, the cheville, and at the other by natural-fibre string in white, cream or beige; slow smoking over resinous wood and sawdust; and production only in the four départements of Franche-Comté, the Jura among them. A sausage smoked with flavouring, or made elsewhere, may look the part. Read the label for the IGP before you pay.
craft:What is sold as Jura-made.why: Look for the wooden peg and the IGP mark together; one without the other is not enough.
facts: Check a 'Morteau' for the cheville at one end, the natural string at the other and the IGP logo on the label
